region: Global South (MENA · Africa · South Asia · LatAm)
partner_context: InDrive is the world's second-most-downloaded ride-hail app, operating in 700+ cities across 45+ countries — and uniquely strong across the Global South markets the Western platforms under-serve: Egypt, Morocco and the wider MENA region, Sub-Saharan Africa (Nigeria, South Africa, Tanzania, Kenya), South Asia (India, Pakistan, Sri Lanka) and Latin America. Its app already owns the urban first/last mile in coastal megacities, resort coasts and island economies where the roads are most congested and the water most under-used.

hero.title: The Global South's challenger-leader ride-hail network — across coasts of resort cities, island ferries and lagoon-choked megacities begging for a clean water layer.
hero.subtitle: Community-priced waterfront legs powered by Navier's electric foiling fleet.

why_now: Foiling lifts the hull clear of the water: faster, dramatically more efficient per passenger-mile, smooth and near-silent, hybrid-capable with no charging-infrastructure dependency, and autonomy-ready. A ~100-vessel network is already ramping in the Maldives (WSJ/Bloomberg, 2026), Singapore's regulator is mandating clean harbour craft from 2030, and Indonesia's most-trafficked crossings (Bali↔Nusa, Batam↔Singapore) are infamous for slow, accident-prone diesel boats. The category gets claimed cluster-by-cluster — and the world's largest archipelago is the surface that matters most.
multimodal_fit: InDrive already routes the first/last mile by car across the Global South's coastal cities. A foiling pier becomes the water node in that same trip graph: InDrive car to the marina or jetty, a clean silent foil across the bay, channel or coast, InDrive car on arrival — one booking, one app, a new mode.
differentiation: Not a niche island-boat play but a massive Global-South opportunity: a new water-mobility vertical layered onto the ride-hail network that already owns coastal demand exactly where the Western apps are thin.

why_navier_now.step_change: Hydrofoiling lifts the hull clear of the water, so a Navier vessel flies instead of plowing through chop - roughly 10x more efficient than a conventional planing boat, faster (30+ kt cruise), and dramatically smoother and quieter. It's software-defined and autonomy-ready, so the same fleet keeps getting better and cheaper to run over time. A step-change in marine mobility, not an incremental faster boat.
why_navier_now.no_new_infrastructure: Navier rides on infrastructure that already exists - the open ocean and the berths and jetties already in use. No vertiports, no new rights-of-way, no tunnels or tracks. Pioneer II needs only a berth pedestal; the Quanta-LR hybrid needs no charging infrastructure at all. That's the fundamental contrast with flying taxis and other new-infrastructure modes: nothing to permit, build, or wait for.
why_navier_now.the_moment: Three forces just converged across the Global South: InDrive's deep coastal ride-hail demand, severe road congestion and painful overland detours, and marquee crossings (Hurghada↔Sharm, Agadir↔Essaouira, Mumbai↔Alibaug, Zanzibar↔Dar) reachable today only by flights, ferries or all-day drives. A clean foiling layer turns that latent demand into a dispatched mode.

network_thesis.headline: The water layer of the Global South's challenger ride-hail network.

Pioneer II flies the sheltered bays today; the Quanta-LR hybrid opens the long open-water corridors with no charging infrastructure at all.

markets.corridors_note: Journeys we unlock across coastal Africa — the Lagos lagoon, Zanzibar's coast, and Cape Town's bay.

the_ask.navier_brings: The software-defined foiling fleet, captain training, the maintenance & certification path, and a uniform integration spec.
the_ask.partner_brings: Demand, the rider/guest relationship, and Sub-Saharan Africa (Lagos · Cape Town · Zanzibar) as the launch market to prove the on-water tier.
the_ask.next_step: Scope a Phase-1 pilot (~7 vessels) on the entry corridor, building to ~148 vessels as the network matures (addressable ceiling ~370).

journeys_unlocked.with_navier: A ~45-min foiling run, booked in InDrive.
A direct foiling run — no road at all.

proof_points.claim: inDrive already owns the first/last mile in the Global South's coastal megacities.
proof_points.evidence: inDrive is among the world's most-downloaded ride-hail apps, operating in 700+ cities across 45+ countries, uniquely strong exactly where Western platforms are thin — Egypt, Morocco, Nigeria, Tanzania, India and across Latin America.

proof_points.claim: The vessel is commercial today.
proof_points.evidence: The N30 Pioneer II is in commercial service now — 70 nm range, ~30 kt, 6–8 passengers — already operating with the Four Seasons on Lake Austin. Delivery-ready, not a concept.

proof_points.claim: A network at scale is already being built.
proof_points.evidence: Navier is ramping a roughly 100-vessel water network in the Maldives with JIH Global over three years and signed a national agreement with WorldBridge in Cambodia in May 2026.

proof_points.claim: Foiling economics fit a value-led app.
proof_points.evidence: Hydrofoiling cuts energy per passenger-mile dramatically, and the Quanta-LR hybrid needs no charging infrastructure — the cost base a challenger network can run, not just a luxury charter.

objections.concern: Will this work in markets with weak marine infrastructure?
objections.response: Navier rides on infrastructure that already exists — open water and the jetties already in use. Pioneer II needs only a berth pedestal and the Quanta-LR needs no charging at all, so launch doesn't wait on new ports.

objections.concern: Our riders are price-sensitive — is a water tier too premium?
objections.response: The lagoon commute in Lagos or the harbour crossing in Mumbai isn't a luxury — it's hours of gridlock today. Foiling's efficiency is what lets a faster water option sit inside a value-led app, with resort corridors funding the launch.

Most crossings here are short — Lagos lagoon ~6 nm, Mumbai↔Alibaug ~11 nm, El Gouna↔Hurghada ~12 nm — inside the all-electric Pioneer II envelope. The Quanta-LR hybrid covers the longer legs (Gulf of Suez, Agadir↔Essaouira, Zanzibar↔Dar) up to 700 nm.

objections.concern: Why boats for a ride-hail app?
objections.response: You bring demand, dispatch, wallet and brand; Navier brings the fleet, captains and maintenance — the same split that works for cars, applied to the one surface no Global South platform has digitized.

end_state.headline: The water layer of the Global South's challenger ride-hail network.
end_state.addressable_footprint: Every coastal market inDrive already serves where lagoons, gulfs or island ferries sit offshore — the Egyptian Red Sea, Morocco's Atlantic, Mumbai and the Konkan, and the Lagos–Cape Town–Zanzibar arc of Sub-Saharan Africa.

steady_state.total_markets: 4+ coastal clusters across MENA, Africa & South Asia
steady_state.platform_mix: Pioneer II commute capillaries + Quanta-LR coastal crossings
steady_state.tam_framing: Tens of millions of lagoon commutes and resort crossings a year, today lost to gridlock and slow ferries, moved into the inDrive app.

end_state.narrative: Steady state is the coastal map of inDrive's footprint. Start where the pain is sharpest — the Lagos lagoon, the Mumbai harbour, the Red Sea coast — prove the in-app water tier, then extend across the Global South coastline the incumbents overlook.

the_ask.navier_brings: The software-defined foiling fleet (Pioneer II + Quanta-LR), captain training, maintenance and the network operating system.
the_ask.partner_brings: Demand and dispatch through the inDrive app, the wallet, the brand, and the choice of launch city.
the_ask.next_step: Scope a first pilot in one flagship city — Lagos or Hurghada — co-defining the in-app water tier on three corridors.

close.title: One app. The Global South's coasts. A surface the incumbents ignore.
close.body: inDrive already owns demand where the West is thin. Water is the one transport surface still served by gridlock and slow ferries. Start in a single lagoon or gulf, prove the foiling tier, and scale it across the coastlines inDrive already leads.
